correctness.rationale: The universal upper witnesses are valid for every real p-Banach space by the p-triangle inequality. The sharp lower witness is the canonical free p-space of the equilateral triple, whose three spanning-tree norm is the explicit published formula [2]. The Banach free-space contraction excludes centers outside the affine simplex by radius >2. On the simplex the largest of three radii reduces to 2(b^p+c^p)^(1/p), where a<=b<=c; strict concavity for 0<p<1 gives only vertices or the barycenter, with crossover 3^p=2; p=1 is checked independently. All endpoint and equality cases have been accounted for. Exact-rational and floating grid tests merely supplement this analytic proof.

value.rationale: The symmetric three-leaf star is a canonical finite one-point extension problem where the nonlocally convex geometry can be computed completely. The sharp phase threshold log(2)/log(3), its exact 3/4/1 optimizing-center multiplicity, and a p-independent low-exponent plateau make a structurally meaningful distinction between nearest-leaf and barycentric extension strategies. The result bridges a known generic finite free p-norm algorithm and a 2024 motivating three-point extension problem while furnishing a nontrivial universal sharp constant rather than a routine arithmetic instance.
